summary: GAME-RENDER-ADOPT-01.2 (Game#746, Outcome .github#5179). Harness: tests/Render.Browser.Bench (Fable page; BenchGame<'State> plug-in = Init, deterministic Step, Width/Height, scenes whose View returns exactly `size` drawable nodes; ReferenceGame's real Composition.Model via src/ReferenceGame/Program.fs, whose Harness-only parts sit under #if !FABLE_COMPILER), instrument.js (WebGL draw-call counter, rAF callback time, per-callback EXT_disjoint_timer_query_webgl2 TIME_ELAPSED summed per frame), tools/render-bench/driver.mjs (Node built-in WebSocket CDP, no npm dependency; one fresh browser per run; capacity probe before each run; ABBA repeat order; COOP/COEP for a 5 us page clock). Each run presents through RendererRegistry + RendererMsg.SelectBackend/StateChanged and refuses a backend that is not mounted/Active, a scene whose node count differs, or a GPU-mode run whose backend context reports a software renderer. Measured, not inferred: frame time p50/p95/p99 (uncapped pacing: --disable-gpu-vsync --disable-frame-rate-limit), main-thread CPU (CDP ThreadTime), GPU/renderer process CPU (SystemInfo.getProcessInfo), GPU time (WebGL backends only; SVG Unknown), draw calls (WebGL only; SVG Unknown), JS heap after forced GC, drawn-node coverage. Lessons: (1) a timer query left open across frames measures the GPU-timeline frame period, not busy time; bracket each callback. (2) Babylon adapter draws only part of scenes above ~400 nodes (per-index depth under a perspective camera; Game#753); its rows are coverage-partial and not comparable. (3) Babylon renders twice per frame (sync render in Present plus render loop). (4) An orphaned uncapped benchmark browser spins a core; the driver kills its process groups on exit/signals. fdev facts observed 2026-11-01 with Chrome for Testing 153.0.8010.12 (Playwright chromium-1243, private LD_LIBRARY_PATH libs): headless --use-angle=vulkan --enable-features=Vulkan --ignore-gpu-blocklist gives WebGL/WebGL2 on 'ANGLE (AMD, Vulkan 1.4.354 (AMD Ryzen 9 7900 12-Core Processor (RADV RAPHAEL_MENDOCINO) (0x0000164E)), radv)' with chrome://gpu webgl/gpu_compositing/rasterization 'enabled' (rasterization not forced) and timer queries; --use-gl=angle --use-angle=gl-egl gives radeonsi; plain --use-angle=gl gives no WebGL. WebGPU is available (amd/rdna-2, not fallback, timestamp-query) but only on a secure origin: a data: URL hides navigator.gpu, which explains the earlier 'WebGPU Unknown' in environment/fdev-gpu-and-audio. No virtual display (Xvfb/Wayland) was needed or installed. Limits: virtio-gpu native context onto the Home host's shared integrated AMD GPU, headless, no scanout; not B1-B8 or bare-metal Home evidence. Baseline numbers live in tools/render-bench/baselines and the README, not here.
title: FS.GG.Game rendering benchmark: CDP-driven Chromium over the RendererSelection route, fsgg.render-bench/v1 results, fdev GPU and software baselines
